AI._PricingNotes: USD per million tokens, verified against https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing on 2026-09-30. CacheWritePerMTok is the 5-minute-cache rate — every ClaudeService cache_control breakpoint omits an explicit ttl, so it always uses the 5-minute cache, never the 1-hour rate. CacheReadPerMTok is 0.1x input for all four models below (none of them get the 0.025x/0.05x discounted-read rate that only applies to Fable 5.1/Mythos 5.1/Opus 5.5). claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 is this repo's actual Claude:FreeModel value, which carries a date suffix Anthropic's current docs do not list under that name (only 'claude-haiku-4-5' is documented) — priced here at the same Haiku 4.5 rates on the assumption it is a still-valid dated snapshot, but see the Phase 1 model-string verification note; this entry should be corrected or removed once that is confirmed against the live Models API.
AI._RoutingNotes: AI routing Phase 3 (docs pasted plan): Models/Capabilities are the router's config seam — every value below reproduces today's actual ClaudeService/DetectionService behaviour exactly (temperature constants, per-call max_tokens, HTTP client timeouts), verified against the live source at the time this was written. Models.Writing/Fast/Reasoning are deliberately OMITTED (not set to null) so they fall back to Claude:Model/Claude:FreeModel/Claude:Model respectively, identical to what ClaudeService already resolves — the JSON config binder turns an explicit `null` on a string property into an empty string, not a true null, so AiModelRouter's Coalesce() helper also treats empty as unset defensively, but the config itself avoids the literal to begin with. Only Model is actually enforced today (via the existing modelOverride parameter); Temperature/MaxOutputTokens/Timeout are accurate metadata, not yet wired to control a Claude request — see AiPolicy's doc comment. TierSensitive=true reproduces the Phase 2 Free-tier override per capability; Detect is TierSensitive=false because DetectionService reads Claude:Model directly today with no Free-tier branch at all.
AI._MaxInputTokensNotes: AI routing Phase 5: derived from each tool's existing real input ceiling (its DTO/validator char cap ÷ 4, rounded up with headroom) — see the Phase 5 audit. Humanise/Paraphrase/Detect have no chunking, so this is a near-duplicate of their existing validator cap (defense in depth, now token-based and router-configurable). GrammarCheck/Summarise already chunk long input, so their MaxInputTokens is set generously above normal chunked use — it exists only as an outer sanity ceiling against genuine abuse, never to interfere with legitimate chunked requests.

FairUse._Notes: AI routing Phase 5: PLACEHOLDER values only — real numbers to be supplied. Sums AiCallLog.EstimatedCost per user across the current UTC day/calendar month, regardless of call Status (Success/Failed/Cancelled/Interrupted all count — a failed or cancelled call can still have spent real tokens). Blocks further calls for that user once either ceiling is reached; the controlled error message never states a dollar figure.

Retry._Notes: AI routing Phase 6: standardises what Claude:RetryCount already controlled for the Claude/Detector HttpClients (DependencyInjection.cs). Both keys fall back to today's actual values if omitted — MaxAttempts to Claude:RetryCount (3), BaseDelayMs to 1000 (which reproduces the old hardcoded '2^n seconds' backoff formula exactly: BaseDelayMs * 2^attempt). Set here explicitly to the same values the fallbacks already produce — no behaviour change, just now visible/editable under one config path.

EssayRunner._Notes: The separate essay service (essay-runner, port 8007). Off by default: set Enabled true to have web-sourced essays written by it. If it is down or busy and FallbackToBuiltIn is true the built-in pipeline writes the essay instead. Secret must match ESSAY_RUNNER_SECRET on the service when that is set.

DeepResearch._Notes: Every value is a starting point to be replaced by telemetry (AiCallLog, Seq 'DeepResearch.*'); none is a product promise. A request may tighten these limits, never raise them.
